_about: Reviewed split decisions for content rows whose misconceptions text has more than one clause (Q16, 16 Nov 2026). A decision applies only while the row text is exactly the same; otherwise the rules in shared/science-items.ts apply and the row is reported.

C1-DAN-004.text: All big animals are wild animals. Wild animals live only in jungles.

C1-DME-004.text: Our body stops changing once we start school. When teeth fall out, they never grow back.

C1-DSU-009.text: Deserts are full of water. Every desert is hot and sandy.

C1-DWA-008.text: Clear water is always safe to drink. Any filter makes water safe.

C3-02-003.text: Only fast buses are dangerous; a slow bus cannot hurt anyone.
C3-02-003.note: one idea: the second clause restates the first

C3-06-029.text: Planting a sapling once is enough; it needs no care.
C3-06-029.note: one idea: the second clause restates the first

C3-06-039.text: The painted stork flies to India each winter from cold countries. Siberian cranes still come to India every winter.

C3-08-026.text: A potato is a root. An onion is just a stem.

C3-10-005.text: All metals are found lying ready-made on the ground. (Most are not, though a few, like gold, can be found as pure bits.)
items: All metals are found lying ready-made on the ground.
C3-10-005.note: the bracket is the correction, not a misconception; item = the first sentence only

C3-11-008.text: All bricks are cut from rocks. (Baked bricks are moulded from mud; only in some places, such as Kerala, are blocks of laterite stone cut and used like bricks.)
items: All bricks are cut from rocks.
C3-11-008.note: the bracket is the correction, not a misconception; item = the first sentence only

C3-12-001.text: Only factories make waste; homes do not.
C3-12-001.note: one idea: the second clause restates the first

C4-02-002.text: A town must choose either new roads or trees; it cannot have both.
C4-02-002.note: one idea: the second clause restates the first

C5-04-016.text: Litter only looks ugly; it does no harm.
C5-04-016.note: one idea: the second clause restates the first

C5-DPL-064.text: Before J.C. Bose, nobody knew that plants were living things.

C6-01-008.text: Anything written in a science book is fixed forever; or, if an idea changes, science has failed.

C6-01-019.text: Everyone's normal temperature is exactly 37 °C at all times; in fact it varies slightly from person to person and through the day.
items: Everyone's normal temperature is exactly 37 °C at all times.
C6-01-019.note: "; in fact …" is the correction, not a misconception; item = the first clause only

C6-01-023.text: The Sun is not a star; or, stars are tiny points of light much smaller than the Sun.

C6-02-035.text: Bats are birds; whales are fish.

C6-02-044.text: Herbs are only plants used in cooking or medicine; tall plants cannot be herbs.
C6-02-044.note: one idea or two? ("herbs are only cooking or medicine plants" / "tall plants cannot be herbs"); kept whole

C6-02-080.text: Every flying animal is a bird; birds fly using only their wings.

C6-02-091.text: Invertebrates are always tiny. All invertebrates have soft bodies.

C6-02-116.text: Grasses have no flowers. Mushrooms are non-flowering plants.

C6-04-008.text: Only factories can make magnets; a piece of soft iron magnetised by a magnet stays a magnet for ever.

C6-04-028.text: There is a huge bar magnet buried inside the Earth; or, a compass points to the exact geographic North Pole.

C6-10-012.text: Plants do not respire; they only make oxygen.
C6-10-012.note: one idea: the second clause explains the first

C6-DAN-003.text: An organ is made of only one kind of cell; nerves from the brain start every heartbeat.

C6-DEN-025.text: Used batteries belong in the blue bin along with plastic and glass; paper and cardboard go in the green (wet) bin.

C6-DPL-003.text: Only roots and leaves do any work; the stem just stands there.
C6-DPL-003.note: one idea: the second clause restates the first
